prompt: A plumber charges a flat call-out fee of $\$75$ plus $\$45$ for each hour of work. A customer's total bill was $\$322.50$. How many hours did the plumber work?
hint: One number is charged once; the other is charged per hour. Build $75 + 45h = 322.50$.

hints.text: One number is charged once; the other is charged per hour. Build $75 + 45h = 322.50$.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try smaller numbers first: a $\$10$ fee plus $\$5$ per hour, with a $\$35$ bill. Subtract the fee ($\$25$ left) and divide by the rate: $5$ hours. The real problem is the same two steps.

learningObjective: Model a flat-fee-plus-rate situation and solve for the rate quantity.
explanation: The flat fee is paid once and the hourly rate is paid $h$ times, so the total is $75 + 45h$.
Set that equal to the bill: $75 + 45h = 322.50$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Reason without algebra
steps: Of the $\$322.50$ bill, $\$75$ was not for labour, so $\$247.50$ was.
At $\$45$ per hour, $\$225$ buys 5 hours and $\$22.50$ buys half an hour.
That is $5.5$ hours — the same answer, reached by splitting the money rather than by solving.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: Dividing the whole bill by the rate — 322.50 ÷ 45 ≈ 7.2 hours — silently bills the call-out fee as labour, and 7.2 will be a choice.
The fee is paid once, so it comes OFF the bill before any dividing. Fixed charge first, rate second, every time.
